Proof of concept · Update 2

Day-ahead solar and wind forecasts from public Philippine data

A forecast of every solar and wind unit in the Philippine electricity market, built only on the market's public schedules and free weather forecasts, and scored against the market's own day-ahead schedule.

Prepared by: Rogelio Ruzcko Tobias
Last updated: 2026-11-09

84 units modelled4,196 MWTest: 15 October–8 November 2026Public data only
Overview

A pretrained model beats the market's day-ahead schedule for solar. Wind is not there yet.

The project archives the market's public 5-minute schedules every day, places 93 of 114 solar and wind units on a map, and forecasts each unit's next-day output from free weather forecasts. Four models were compared over the same 24-day test: two tree models trained on the project's data, and two pretrained time-series models used as published. Chronos-2, with no training on this data, has the lowest solar fleet error, below the market's own day-ahead schedule. For wind, the market schedule is still better than every model.

Reading the numbers. Error is nMAE: the average absolute error divided by installed capacity. On the solar fleet, Chronos-2's 2.7% is about 99 MW off in an average daylight hour. Fleet errors are lower than unit errors because errors at different plants partly cancel. "Actual" is the market's real-time schedule, which follows plant output closely but is not metered output.

Need and criteria

The market publishes schedules for every solar and wind unit, but no open forecast of their output. The question for this proof of concept: can public data alone forecast each unit's output for the next day, about as well as the market's own day-ahead schedule?

What changed in this update

  • 7 November 2026. Daily archive of the market's public files started; it keeps history the market site drops after about 90 days.
  • 7 November 2026. Plant table: 114 solar and wind units with towns and coordinates; data check of every unit.
  • 8 November 2026. Day-ahead weather forecasts pulled for 76 plant locations from 1 August 2026.
  • 8 November 2026. First model trained and scored; tilted-panel sunshine added after the first run under-forecast solar.
  • 8 November 2026. Three more models scored on the same test: LightGBM, trained like the first model, and the pretrained Chronos-2 and Timestral, used without training on this data. The hourly viewer shows all four and has an hour slider.
  • 9 November 2026. The tree models now also see each unit's output up to noon the day before, the same information as the pretrained models. Solar results barely moved.
Results

Forecasts against the real-time schedule

Every forecast is scored on the same units, hours and days. The market's day-ahead schedule is the latest run issued by noon the day before. Solar is scored from 07:00 to 18:00, wind on all hours. Times are Philippine time.

Hourly forecasts

    How to read this chart

    Each line is megawatts at the end of the hour. The dark line is the real-time schedule, used here as actual output. The buttons above the chart show or hide each line. Move the slider under the chart, or tap or point at the chart, to pick one hour: the list under the slider gives every shown line's value at that hour and each forecast's error against actual. Solar units are zero at night; those hours are not scored. The error line at the bottom uses the same scoring as the rest of the report, for the week and series shown.

    Data

    Public market schedules, archived every day

    The Independent Electricity Market Operator of the Philippines (IEMOP) publishes the market's schedules as files on its website [1], but keeps only about 90 days. The archive has saved them daily since 7 August 2026: 5-minute schedules for 577 generating units.

    ForecastAdd weather, train or run the four models and score them.weather.py · model.py · foundation.py

    Registered capacity (CAPEG)Daily maximum capacity per unitCapacity for scoring

    Plant locations

    The plant table lists 114 units (102 solar, 12 wind). 93 have coordinates: 63 from a mapped plant outline (high confidence), 22 from a town matched to the unit name (medium) and 8 from a weaker name hint (low). The other 21 have no location yet.

    Which units are usable

    91 solar and 10 wind units pass the data check; 13 do not. A unit is dropped when its day-ahead schedule is empty, its schedule repeats every day, it sits at zero for more than 7 days, or its capacity factor is below 5%. The check also scores the market's day-ahead schedule over the whole archive:

    Market forecasts over the archive, 7 August–8 November 2026, usable units (nMAE)
    FleetUnitsMWDay-ahead, fleetYesterday, fleetDay-ahead, median unitYesterday, median unitUnits where day-ahead is better
    Solar91.04,0683.7%4.5%10.3%10.5%61.0
    Wind10.05544.8%9.8%10.5%15.3%7.0

    For a single solar unit, the market's day-ahead schedule is barely better than repeating yesterday. That gap is the room a weather-driven forecast can use.

    Time conventions
    • Market schedules give the MW target at the end of each interval. Forecasts are therefore compared with the on-the-hour value, not an hourly average.
    • The market day-ahead baseline for day D is the latest DAP run issued at or before 12:00 on D−1.
    • Midnight timestamps in the market files carry no clock time; they are read as 00:00.
    • All times are Philippine time (UTC+8).
    Model

    Two trained models and two pretrained models

    Each trained model is a gradient-boosted tree ensemble (scikit-learn's HistGradientBoosting [7] or LightGBM [9]) shared by all units of its type, with the unit as a category. It predicts output as a share of capacity, from inputs that are known the day before.

    Four models

    HistGB

    scikit-learn's histogram gradient boosting [7]: one model per type, pooled over its units, retrained every week. It also sees each unit's output up to noon the day before.

    Trained on project data · 600 trees · weekly retrain

    LightGBM

    The same inputs, rows and weekly schedule as HistGB, with LightGBM's leaf-wise trees [9].

    Trained on project data · 600 trees · weekly retrain

    Chronos-2

    Pretrained by Amazon on many public time series [10]; not trained on this project's data. It sees each unit's output up to noon the day before, and the weather forecasts and sun position as inputs known for the forecast hours.

    Pretrained · zero-shot · median forecast · 120M parameters

    Timestral

    Pretrained by Mistral AI and released in October 2026 [11]; not trained on this project's data. It gets the same inputs as Chronos-2.

    Pretrained · zero-shot · median forecast · 28M parameters

    Inputs

    Weather

    Day-ahead forecasts from ECMWF IFS at 0.25° [3] and NOAA GFS [4] at 76 plant locations: sunshine (direct, diffuse and total), cloud cover, temperature, and wind speed at 10 m and 100 m, plus wind direction.

    Sun and panel

    Sun elevation, clear-sky sunshine and the sun's angle to a south-facing panel tilted 15°, from standard solar-position formulas [8]. Forecast sunshine is turned into sunshine on that tilted panel.

    Recent behaviour

    Each unit's average output over the 7 days ending two days before, and its recent output per unit of forecast panel sunshine. Both adapt to season, soiling and curtailment. Also its output up to noon the day before: the latest hour, the 07:00–12:00 average, and that average per unit of forecast panel sunshine.

    Training

    From the start of the test, both trained models are retrained every week on everything known two days before that week, then score the week. Training starts on 7 August 2026.

    Why the panel angle matters

    The first run under-forecast solar. Fleet output per unit of forecast flat-ground sunshine rose from 0.71 in August to 0.98 in November, because tilted panels catch more of the lower autumn sun. On a 15° tilted panel the rise shrinks to 0.72–0.89, and the recent-output ratio absorbs the rest. The remaining bias is −3.7% for HistGB and +1.3% for the market day-ahead schedule.

    Model settings

    HistGradientBoostingRegressor(max_iter=600, learning_rate=0.04, max_leaf_nodes=31, min_samples_leaf=40, l2_regularization=1.0, random_state=2026) and LGBMRegressor(n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.04, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=40, reg_lambda=1.0, random_state=2026). Predictions are clipped to 0–105% of capacity. Solar trains only on hours with the sun above −2°.

    Limits

    A working proof of concept, with clear limits

    LimitEffect
    "Actual" is the real-time schedule, not metered outputCurtailment and dispatch decisions are part of the target; true plant output may differ
    The test covers 24 days in one seasonThe northeast monsoon (December–March) and typhoon days are not yet tested
    Forecast lead times differThe weather inputs are forecasts made about 24 hours ahead, so afternoon hours see a newer forecast than one issued by noon the day before; the market day-ahead schedule is 12–36 hours ahead
    21 units have no location and 8 only a weak oneThey are left out or may use the wrong weather
    One weather point per plant, from global modelsLocal clouds and terrain effects on wind are smoothed out
    Open-Meteo's free service is for non-commercial useA commercial use needs a paid plan or direct ECMWF and NOAA data

    Next steps

    1. Match the forecast lead time exactly: weather from model runs available by noon the day before.
    2. Score the average of Chronos-2 and the market day-ahead schedule as a forecast of its own.
    3. Try the larger Timestral models and Chronos-2 fine-tuned on project data.
    4. Extend the test through the northeast monsoon as the archive grows.
    5. Try more weather models (JMA, DWD ICON, ECMWF AIFS) for wind.
    6. Place the 21 unlocated units by matching their output with located neighbours.

    Decision log

    DateDecision
    2026-11-08Retrain weekly on data known two days before each test week.
    2026-11-08Kept tilted-panel sunshine and the recent-output ratio (E2): solar bias fell from about −6% to −3.5%.
    2026-11-08Compared four models on the same rows. Chronos-2 (E5) has the lowest solar fleet error; no model reaches the market schedule for wind. All three new models stay candidates until the lead-time gap is closed.
    2026-11-09Gave the tree models the output the pretrained models see, up to noon the day before (E7, E8). Solar fleet error moved by 0.1 point or less, so it does not explain Chronos-2's lead. Recent-output windows now follow the target day, which removed a one-hour look-ahead at midnight.
    2026-11-07Compare forecasts with the on-the-hour schedule value, because market schedules are end-of-interval targets.
    2026-11-07Excluded 13 units whose data cannot be scored fairly.
    2026-11-07Located plants from OpenStreetMap and town names; the government plant list could not be downloaded by script.
